title: Prove two 3-cycles need ten calls in every address dimension (no new κ)
body:
## Result

**Written proof with finite corroboration in a formal model. No new κ.** The selected conditional exponent stays 62009/20000000.

In `M_2(F2[GL_n(F2)])` (paid call `I + ([g]+[e])N`, `g` a coordinate CNOT, `N` a rank-one binary idempotent, free scalar maps, formal equality), the target `diag([c],[c])` for a coordinate 3-cycle `c`, with every other address coordinate a restored spectator:

- has **no word of length ≤ 9 for every `n ≥ 3`**. For `n ≥ 5` the previous lower bound was the single-cycle cost 6;
- has a word of length 10 or 11 at some `n` only if one exists at `n = 5` with both spectators written and read at least twice, each target coordinate written and read at least twice, (target, spectator) write counts `(6,4)`, `(6,5)` or `(7,4)`, and at least one cross call each way.

So `10 ≤ cost ≤ 12` for every `n ≥ 5`, and exact cost 12 in every dimension is equivalent to excluding that one five-coordinate case. This answers the reduction part of Open next question 1 of James Reed / jwr404's #5379.

Key step: if one call writes coordinate `k`, projecting the product onto group elements that leave row `k` unchanged gives exactly `A(I+N)B`. After augmentation, `I+N` has rank one, while the target is invertible (spectator) or projects to zero (target row). Transposition handles reads. Restriction and quotient homomorphisms remove spectators that are never written or never read. Counting writes then allows at most two live spectators.

## Evidence

`research/two-three-cycles-every-dimension/` contains `PROOF.md` and a standard-library `verify.py`. The verifier checks the lemmas on concrete words:

- all 120 paid calls at `n = 5` are involutions;
- `rank(I+N) = R-1` at `R = 2, 3`;
- the single-write projection identity holds on 150 random `n = 5` words;
- the restriction, quotient and transpose maps hold on 60 random words each;
- the single-write rank consequence holds on all 368,136 reduced `n = 4` words of length ≤ 3 (629,928 cases);
- the 12-call upper word is checked at `n = 5`;
- the counting step yields the three residual profiles;
- a corrupted-projection control is rejected.

Random-word checks exercise the written lemmas; the proof is the claim. The `n = 3` (#5005) and `n = 4` (#5379) exclusions are cited premises, not re-run.

## Reproduce

From the repository root, interpreter `~/git/integer-mult-bounds/.venv/bin/python3.12` (CPython 3.12), standard library only:

```sh
python3.12 -I -W error -B research/two-three-cycles-every-dimension/verify.py
python3.12 -I -O -W error -B research/two-three-cycles-every-dimension/verify.py
python3.12 -B scripts/research_package.py --package research/two-three-cycles-every-dimension
python3.12 -B scripts/check_research_commit.py --package research/two-three-cycles-every-dimension --check-source-history
```

Local results: both direct runs print `PASS_TWO_THREE_CYCLES_EVERY_DIMENSION` in about 4.3 s each. `research_package.py` prints `PASS_REGISTERED_RESEARCH_PACKAGE` (8.7 s total). `check_research_commit.py` prints `PASS_RESEARCH_COMMIT_BYTES`.

## Limitations

- The residual `n = 5`, length 10 and 11 case is not searched. Exact cost 12 for `n ≥ 5` remains open.
- The conclusion covers `R = 2` only. Lemma 1 holds for any register count, but no `R = 3` spectator base case exists.
- This is a formal-model theorem. It gives no native operation, tariff, supplier change or κ change. Independent human and formal proof-kernel review are unclaimed.

## Open next questions

1. Exclude lengths 10 and 11 at `n = 5` with a meet-in-the-middle search restricted to the three write profiles. This would give exact cost 12 in every dimension.
2. Apply the same reduction to a dirty third register, `diag([c],[c],[e])`. It needs `R = 3` base cases beyond #5292, whose length-11 case is open.
3. Find a two-write analogue of the projection lemma that forces three writes per live spectator. That would remove the residual case without search.

## Related open work

No open PR studies two coordinate 3-cycles or address spectators in this model; the related results #4939, #4974, #5005, #5292 and #5379 are merged. No other PR from this account opened since the claim studies this object.

## Credit

Mihir Srivastava (#4939) built the formal model. James Reed / jwr404 proved the `n = 3` and `n = 4` exact costs (#5005, #5379) and posed the question. JoyboyBrian's single-cycle all-dimension reduction (#4974) suggested the restriction step. These are cited, not re-run or audited. The whole-word projection lemma, the read/write counting and the reduction were produced by Nick Petalas.
